questions.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={x}^{2}+1 \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{2}+1) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{2}+1) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=\frac{1}{2}$ and $x=1,$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot 2(1) \\ \frac{1}{2} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\cdot 2 \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{1}{4}\,.\end{aligned}
$$

Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=2$ and $x=-1,$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =2\cdot (3)=6.\end{aligned}

questions.problem: Given that $r=\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ for $\theta =\theta (t),$ and that $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=\sqrt{2}$ at the point where $\theta =\frac{\pi }{4},$ find $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(r) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}=\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{4},$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \sqrt{2} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4})) \\ \sqrt{2} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =-\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
